# php.oct-2026.story.sgit.ai

> A fact-driven, agent-run tracker for CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619: what is established, who said what and when, which numbers add up, what to do about a vulnerable system, and the captured, hashed evidence behind every line.

Site v0.1.0. Data as of 2026-10-22T08:48Z (the latest capture in the evidence vault, commit 379e3d7f172a). Every page below has a markdown twin at the same path with .md; the data behind every page is in data/*.json. The evidence vault is private; its manifest with every hash is data/sources.json.

## The story
- [Front page](https://php.oct-2026.story.sgit.ai/index.md): A fact-driven, agent-run tracker for CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619: what is established, who said what and when, which numbers add up, what to do about a vulnerable system, and the captured, hashed evidence behind every line.
- [The two flaws](https://php.oct-2026.story.sgit.ai/flaws/index.md): What the CVE records, the GitHub advisories and the PHP security team say about php2shell: the bug classes, what was demonstrated, which deployments, which versions, the fix and the temporary mitigations, with the blast-radius questions.
- [Timeline](https://php.oct-2026.story.sgit.ai/timeline/index.md): 59 dated events in the php2shell story, from the 2024 audit through discovery, coordinated disclosure, the leak, the release and the response, every one tied to a captured source.
- [Who found it](https://php.oct-2026.story.sgit.ai/discovery/index.md): Calif, OpenAI and Wiz each claim the discovery of php2shell; their own timelines side by side, the 2024 audit that saw it first, the credits on the advisories, and what the sources do and do not say about the models.
- [How disclosure broke](https://php.oct-2026.story.sgit.ai/leak/index.md): Hour by hour from the first circulation of the CVE IDs on 20 October to the release on 21 October: the pre-announcement, the deleted video, the early WAF rules, the embargo break, the first attempts, and the three accounts that disagree on what leaked.
- [Exploitation signals](https://php.oct-2026.story.sgit.ai/exploitation/index.md): Every signal of php2shell exploitation in the captured sources, from an Amazon honeypot hit on 17 October to the KEV catalog, with what exploitation would look like on a host.
- [If you run PHP](https://php.oct-2026.story.sgit.ai/playbook/index.md): Inventory, patch, mitigate, shield, isolate or take offline, look for compromise, verify: every agency's php2shell advice merged into one ordered list with the sentence each step comes from.

## The evidence
- [Every claim](https://php.oct-2026.story.sgit.ai/claims/index.md): 49 claims about php2shell, each with who makes it, a status (confirmed, reported, disputed, contradicted or unverified) and the captured sources behind it.
- [The numbers](https://php.oct-2026.story.sgit.ai/numbers/index.md): Every scale figure in circulation about php2shell, with what it measures, who said it, whether anyone checked it, and why they differ by four orders of magnitude.
- [The agencies](https://php.oct-2026.story.sgit.ai/agencies/index.md): The NSA, CISA, the UK NCSC, CERT-EU, ENISA, CERT-FR, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, the Netherlands, Italy, Switzerland, Latvia, Japan, Spain and Portugal on php2shell: who says take it offline, who says isolate, who says patch and nothing more, and who has seen exploitation.
- [Affected systems](https://php.oct-2026.story.sgit.ai/affected/index.md): Which PHP versions and SAPIs php2shell affects, which applications had RCE demonstrated, and the NCSC-NL inventory of 674 products counted by status.
- [Software inventory](https://php.oct-2026.story.sgit.ai/affected/software.md): Every row of the NCSC-NL php2shell software inventory at commit cca173c64ec5, with its status per CVE.
- [Every source](https://php.oct-2026.story.sgit.ai/sources/index.md): The manifest of the php2shell evidence vault: every captured source with its publisher, kind, publication time, capture times, HTTP status and the SHA-256 of every captured file.
- [As a graph](https://php.oct-2026.story.sgit.ai/graph/index.md): 151 nodes and 215 citation edges from the php2shell claims and timeline to the captured sources, drawn from the same rows as the text, with the JSON to download.

## About
- [The method](https://php.oct-2026.story.sgit.ai/method/index.md): How this site keeps evidence: the private vault and its protocol, the five status words, the deterministic build, the gate, and how an agent adds a source or replicates the whole thing for the next incident.
- [The team](https://php.oct-2026.story.sgit.ai/team/index.md): Who does what on this site: the editor, the seven-step pipeline from URL to published claim, each agent role with the rule it enforces and the mistake behind it, and the six audiences.
- [The billing model](https://php.oct-2026.story.sgit.ai/billing/index.md): How this site is paid for: the reading meter that runs (pence per page, kept in your browser, never blocking), the provenance pricing that is designed (per claim, with a share for the fact creator), and a counted model of what the story cost to assemble.
- [Your reading account](https://php.oct-2026.story.sgit.ai/account/index.md): The balance, history and receipts of your reading on this site, kept in your browser.
- [The brief](https://php.oct-2026.story.sgit.ai/brief/index.md): The brief this site was built from, published in full: the editor's written request and two transcribed voice memos on mapping the PHP vulnerability as evidence.
- [Corrections](https://php.oct-2026.story.sgit.ai/corrections/index.md): Where the brief or a page of this site was wrong, what was found and what was done instead.
- [Release history](https://php.oct-2026.story.sgit.ai/admin/versions.md): Every release of this site, with what changed, why, and the vault commit it was built from.
- [Admin & engineering](https://php.oct-2026.story.sgit.ai/admin/index.md): How this site is built, the checks in its gate, where things are, the reality file and the honest column.

## Status words
- confirmed: two or more primary sources agree, or the fact was counted from a captured file
- reported: one party says so, and it has not been contradicted
- disputed: the sources disagree, and both readings are shown
- contradicted: a primary source says otherwise
- unverified: even the reporting outlet could not check it
